result:
Only the new test file was added (the pre-existing deletion of `ConstructorUtilsTest.java` was already present before I started, per the initial git status).

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/reflect/ConstructorUtilsAgentTest.java` — 36 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering `ConstructorUtils`'s public API:

- `getAccessibleConstructor` (both overloads): exact-match semantics, null-arg NPE, non-public class/declaring-class returns null, returns the same accessible `Constructor` instance.
- `getMatchingAccessibleConstructor`: exact match, assignment-compatible match, autoboxing-driven best-fit selection between overloaded constructors, varargs matching, no-match/non-public → null, null-arg NPE.
- `invokeConstructor` (both overloads): overload selection by inferred/explicit types, varargs (including empty), null args/parameter-types treated as empty, `NoSuchMethodException`, `InstantiationException` (abstract class), `InvocationTargetException` (with cause/message asserted).
- `invokeExactConstructor` (both overloads): exact-type requirement (rejects autoboxing that `invokeConstructor` accepts), varargs via explicit array type, `NoSuchMethodException` cases.

Verified with `mvn test -Dtest=ConstructorUtilsAgentTest`: 36/36 pass, no other files touched. Some tricky JDK reflection semantics (e.g., that `Class.getConstructor()` doesn't match varargs/autoboxing exactly, and `invokeExactConstructor` doesn't pack loose args into a varargs array the way `invokeConstructor` does) were verified empirically with throwaway scratch programs before asserting on them.
